subject: Compliance recap — audit log retention window, DPA items, pen-test coordination
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Chen <olivia@bluehorizonpayments.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-11-08T15:12:00-08:00
Subject: Compliance recap — audit log retention window, DPA items, pen-test coordination

Hi Olivia / Samir,

Thanks for taking the time earlier today — helpful conversation. Below is a short recap so we have a single source of truth and actionable next steps. Please flag anything I got wrong or omitted.

Summary of what we heard (pain & goals):
- Audit log retention: you need immutable audit logs covering API calls + user-level actions; canonical ask is 13 months for transactional logs, 7 years for aggregated reports (finance/regulatory).
- SOC 2: SOC 2 Type II report is required for procurement review; you also want a concise summary of controls that map to audit log generation and retention.
- DPA & redlines: legal wants some DPA adjustments around data retention and subprocessors (particularly for our hosted mode + optional private deployment).
- Pen test: you’d like a vendor-initiated pentest window and a template for scope and approved testers.
- Isolation/keys: KMS integration and ability to restrict model training on customer data were noted as gating items.

What we committed to supply by next week (proposed):
1) SOC 2 extract PDF (controls map focused on logging & access) — attached: BHPay_SOC2-summary.pdf
2) Audit log retention matrix that maps event types to retention windows and retention enforcement points — attached: auditlog_retention_matrix.csv
3) Draft DPA with our suggested redlines (initial pass) — attached: draft_DPA_redlines_20271108.pdf
4) Pen-test coordination doc: proposed window options + scope checklist (we will propose dates once you confirm approved testers)

Proposed next steps / owners: 
- Blue Horizon: confirm retention windows for each event class (transactional, auth, admin, aggregated) and any regulatory hold requirements — action: Olivia / Samir — due: 2027-11-10
- Redwood: share SOC2 extract + retention matrix + initial DPA redlines — owner: Marcus — due: 2027-11-10 (attached)
- Technical deep-dive: schedule a 60-min session to walk the audit log schema, access controls, and KMS workflow — suggested slot: 2027-11-12 or 2027-11-15 — owner: Irene / Marcus
- Pen-test scheduling: once BHPay confirms allowed tester list, Redwood will propose two windows — owner: Rachel / BHPay security

Open questions we have for you:
- Do you require WORM (write once read many) storage for audit logs, or is logical immutability sufficient (signed log entries + append-only storage)?
- For data subject retention (individual-level records) vs aggregated metrics, can you confirm different retention periods?

Thanks again — attaching the materials we discussed.

Best,
Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marcus@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0142

Attachments: BHPay_SOC2-summary.pdf (pdf), auditlog_retention_matrix.csv (csv), draft_DPA_redlines_20271108.pdf (pdf)

From: Olivia Chen <olivia@bluehorizonpayments.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Rao <samir@bluehorizonpayments.com>
Date: 2027-11-09T09:04:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Compliance recap — audit log retention window, DPA items, pen-test coordination

Marcus — thanks for the clear recap and the attachments, they look useful. Quick clarifications from our side after sharing with security/legal: 

1) Retention windows: transactional logs = 13 months (firm), aggregated reports = 7 years (we reconcile annually for regulators). Admin/auth logs = 24 months.

2) WORM requirement: Compliance prefers WORM for raw audit logs where feasible, but we can accept logical immutability if you provide cryptographic signing and chain-of-custody evidence. We'll mark this as "preferred" not an immediate blocker.

3) DPA: legal flagged two items — subprocessors list needs explicitness for cloud infra and for any third-party monitoring agents; plus stronger deletion timelines for backups. We'll send redline comments by EOD 2027-11-10.

4) Pen-test: we have an approved vendor list (will attach). Preferred window: Nov 29–Dec 3 or Dec 13–17. Scope: external-facing APIs + drift checks on access policies; we will coordinate a separate NDA if needed.

One more ask: can you confirm whether audit logs exported for our SIEM will contain user identifiers or only hashed IDs by default? Security will want to know about PII in logs.

Olivia
Head of Security Operations | Blue Horizon Payments
olivia@bluehorizonpayments.com

From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Chen <olivia@bluehorizonpayments.com>, Samir Rao <samir@bluehorizonpayments.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-11-09T10:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Compliance recap — audit log retention window, DPA items, pen-test coordination

Olivia — appreciate the quick turn. A few actionable clarifications from Redwood: 

- Exported logs for SIEM: configurable. Default export includes user email and an internal user_id. We can toggle to mask/hash email fields before export if you need PII removed. We'll note that in the retention matrix.
- WORM vs logical immutability: we support both patterns depending on deployment. In our hosted API we provide cryptographic signing + append-only storage; in Private deployments we can enable WORM-backed object storage if required.
- Subprocessors: we'll include the infra and monitoring agents explicitly in the DPA redline.

Next steps (updated):
1) Marcus will post an updated retention matrix that explicitly shows which fields are present in exports and whether they're masked — ETA: 2027-11-10 EOD.
2) Marcus & Irene — propose two technical deep-dive times: 2027-11-12 10:00 PT or 2027-11-15 14:00 PT. Please confirm which works.
3) Olivia/Samir — share approved pen-test vendor list and confirm preferred window (either Nov 29–Dec 3 or Dec 13–17).

If helpful, I can also schedule a 30-min session with our compliance engineer to walk legal’s redlines live.

Thanks — Rachel
